question: Which of the pairs of quantities can be expressed using the same unit?
solution:
**__Concept:__**

**Power** is defined as the time rate at which work is done or energy is transferred. Power, like work and energy, is a scalar quantity.

__
 
• Its dimensions are [ML²T⁻³].
 
• In the SI, its unit is called a **watt (W)**. The watt is Js⁻¹.

**Momentum (p)**: The product of mass and velocity is called momentum.

 
• Momentum (p) = mass (m) × velocity (v)
 
• The SI unit of momentum is kg m/s

**Impulse: **When a large force works on a body for a very small time interval, it is called** impulsive force.**

 
• An **impulsive **force does not remain constant, but changes first from zero to maximum and then from maximum to zero. In such a case, we measure the total effect of force.

​vec I = mathop smallint limits{ₜ₁}{t_²} vec F · dt

Where, I = impulse, F = force and dt = very small time interval

 
• SI unit of impulse is **Newton-second** or **kg-m-s⁻¹**.

**Potential energy** is defined as the **energy stored due to change in position relative to others**, stresses within itself, or many factors.

 
• The** potential energy (U) = m g h** [where m= mass of body, g= acceleration due to gravity, h = distance from the ground].
 
• The **Dimension of energy** is - **ML²T⁻²**
 
• The SI unit of energy is Joule (J)

**Acceleration:** The **rate of change of velocity** is called **acceleration**.

 
• It is denoted by a.
 
• The SI unit of acceleration **m/s².**

**Weight: **The weight (w) of an object is the force of gravity on the object and may be defined as the mass (m) times the acceleration of gravity (g).

 
• Weight is a force, the SI unit of weight is** Newton.**
 
• **Weight (W) = m g**

**Work done: **Work is said to be done when a force applied on the body displaces the body through a certain distance in the direction of a force.

 
• Work done ( W ) = vec F · vec scos theta = Fs costheta 
 
• Where F = force, s = distance, and cos θ = angle between F and s.
 
• The **SI unit of work done is N-m or Joule (J)**.

**Kinetic energy (K.E): **The energy possessed by a body by the virtue of its motion is called **kinetic energy.**

 
• The expression for kinetic energy is given by:
 
• K.E = (1)/(2)m{v²}
 
• Where m = mass of the body and v = velocity of the body
 
• The SI unit of energy **is Joule (J).**

**Explanation:__**

As explained above,

 
• Power (Joule -sec) which is not equal to SI unit of Momentum (kg ⋅ m/s)
 
• Impulse (kg ⋅ m/s) which is not equal to SI unit of Potential energy (Joule)
 
• Acceleration (m/s²) which is not equal to SI unit of Weight (Newton)
 
• **Work (Joule) which has equal SI unit as Kinetic Energy (Joule)**
